[b]-- Positives --[/b] • Good gameplay loop • Pretty good music • Looks pretty good. Has an "arcade game" feel with the resolution and screen distortion effect. [b]-- Negatives --[/b] • In the later parts of the game, the visual noise becomes crazy and it becomes hard to see your own drill • Very limited number of game settings, very low number of resolutions, and nothing beyond 1920x1080. • The controls on the Xbox controller are a bit iffy, some of the buttons don't work. [b]-- Notes --[/b] • It's not particularly long, can be beaten in less than 5 hours. • It's very cheap [b]-- Review --[/b] You Know The Drill is the debut title from a solo developer, and it's a pretty good debut game for what it is. It's not very long, but it's also very cheap, and it's simple enough a concept that even children can play it with no trouble. It's one of those games that can keep you entertained for an afternoon by tickling that part of your brain that really likes watching numbers go up, and the numbers most definitely go up and up in this one. You start with a drilling machine that can't run for very long and can't drill very well into the ores you need to collect and sell for upgrades, but as you buy more upgrades that increases the drill's battery, increases the damage the drill does to ore, increases its travel speed, drilling speed, unlocks boost, and also unlocks lasers and drones and rockets and more, the screen get absolutely *buried* in special effects and really large numbers. The flashing colors are certainly very entertaining, but at the same time, it can also be difficult to even see your drill in all the noise. There's also some issues with the controls at the moment, at least on the Xbox Controller. The button to start a new run is bound to the X button, but it doesn't do anything in the game, so I had to use the mouse and click the button on-screen to start every new run. Not a big issue, but I wanted to mention it. For a small, cheap game, this one is alright.

中下水准的增量游戏，初一进游戏的视听反馈让人感觉不错，但是很快就会进入枯燥的重复阶段。看似庞大的天赋树除了4个特殊武器外全是干枯的数值升级，一个背包空间就可以占满天赋树的一整条，来来回回升级几十次。关卡间也没有任何新东西出现，无非是继续膨胀的数值和换换颜色的新矿，终局依然是没有吸引力的重复劳动。整体体验不比对着屏幕发一下午呆好的了多少，就算考虑到价格也不是很推荐。
从游戏性讲，是一款刚及格的增量。不推荐的原因是没有光敏提示，到最后棱彩矿的时候，爆炸的白光，棱彩的动态光，光柱的白光等等，把我眼睛都快闪瞎了，而且最后的升级任务还强制你在这个关卡玩几十分钟，光敏症慎入！！！！

[h1]Good game, bad price.[/h1] You Know The Drill's a Nodebuster-like. You get incrementally stronger with each run as you fill out an upgrade tree until everything is maxed. If you like Nodebuster-likes, this is a good one. If you find them boring, this one isn't going to change your mind. The game's well executed and has a great aesthetic. The core gameplay is fun, most upgrades feel meaningful and satisfying, and though the final level isn't really much different than any of the previous, it does feel good to complete. But the game's short, even if you select the full game option (instead of the faster paced rush option). I felt like I took my time a bit, and it took me just under 2.5 hours to complete and watch credits. If you're playing fully casual and not really trying, this shouldn't take longer than 3 hours. If you're trying to speedrun this game, I'm certain you could get under 2 hours. I hate to see a good game marred by such a short playtime and be overpriced because of it. Many Nodebuster-likes have this issue and You Know The Drill is no exception. It really does feel like it's just long enough to make you ineligible for a refund. I don't expect an endless game, but add a layer of replayability, drop the price to $1.99, or ideally, just add more late/end game content. [b]If you like what you see and are down for a Nodebuster-like that lasts around 2 to 2.5 hours, this game will do you well. However, there is not enough gameplay to justify the full $4.99 price, and so I do not recommend the game unless it's on sale.[/b]

Not Recommended · ~5 hrs (beat both modes) ok so this game is fun for like an hour and then its just a chore. thats the honest verdict. you drill, you sell ore, you buy upgrades that mostly just make you drill faster, repeat that forever until youve unlocked everything and then theres no reason to open it again. thats the whole game. the loop DOES hook you early, watching the upgrade tree grow is nice, but it peaks fast and then just keeps going at the same intensity with no new ideas, no escalation, nothing. and the thing that really got me is whats NOT here.....no story hooks, no stakes, no deadline, no small narrative bits to keep you going, not even an ending cutscene for beating the whole thing. rush mode is sold like a second mode but its basically just the campaign sped up so calling it two modes is generous lol. once the novelty of the first mine wears off youre just grinding upgrades that dont change how the game plays, only how fast it plays. for $4.99 its not a scam or anything and if you literally just want a chill 60 min timekiller youll get that. but its shorter and thinner than the price makes it look and it stops respecting your time after the first hour. if you want this genre done right go find the old flash game Mega Drill (xgen studios), same idea but it had a 25 week deadline, an actual goal, and 5 different endings based on how you did, which gave it replay value this has zero of. motherload is the deeper story version. play either of those instead.

[b]YOU KNOW THE DRILL[/b], is a very typical incremental game. Your usual, timer based, resource nodebuster. You Know The Drill, really isn't anything revolutionary, and feels extremely similar to other space miner incrementals such as Deep Space Cache and Void Miner. The game is paced fairly well and isn't overly grindy, EXCEPT for the end-game. The final goal after you have finished all the nodes was extremely boring. The game is a little buggy on controller especially in regards to the "nitro" mechanic where the inputs it would register to trigger it was extremely inconsistent. All that being said: the game does not over stay its welcome and therefore stays at a pretty fun level almost the whole way through. So, if you know exactly to expect, a nodebuster space mining game, this game is a good one to play. [b]PROS[/b]: - Well paced - Enjoyable lo-fi music - Easy to understand [b]CONS[/b]: - Buggy on controller - Grindy towards the end - Nothing special [i]Ironically, if you know the drill, then definitely worth playing.[/i]

Game is pretty with nice visual effects. Worth the money if you want a decent one time incremental game. Only complaint is that rush mode is quite pointless, since the game isn't replayable in the first place.
